input.rationale: Section 7.5 does contain a transition regime: the Servicer must cooperate in an orderly transition on resignation or termination (p0343) and must transfer funds and deliver the Receivable Files and records to the Successor Servicer (p0344/p0346), with the custodian delivering Receivable Files on termination of that appointment (p0147). However it fails the fallback on two material terms: there is no minimum transition assistance period (no 90 days, or any period), and delivery of files and records is only "as soon as practicable", with no 30-day outside date. We therefore target the fallback with the two shortest conforming edits: a 90-day assistance floor in 7.5(a) and a 30-day delivery deadline in 7.5(b). We have not pursued the preferred position (six months, machine-readable format, certified deletion), which is not required where fallback is met. We note but do not redline the 7.5(b) carve-out (p0346) refusing to license servicing software or provide items restricted by confidentiality or data protection policies; it is directed at Servicer processes and third-party-restricted materials rather than the express Receivable Files and records delivery obligation, and the cost allocation in 7.5(c) sits with the terminated Servicer.

proposal.summary: Add a 90-day transition assistance period and a 30-day outside date for delivery of funds, Receivable Files and records on Servicer resignation or termination.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 7.5 requires cooperation but sets no minimum assistance period and only an open-ended "as soon as practicable" delivery date, so we have added our fallback position: at least 90 days of transition assistance and delivery of the funds, Receivable Files and records within 30 days of the effective date of resignation or termination.
